eyebrow: A FIELD NOTEBOOK FOR CURIOUS MINDS
headline:
Small clues.
Big lake questions.
intro: Become a lake detective. Follow the evidence, collect your ideas, and help your team ask better questions.
lakeNote: Lady Bird Lake is a narrow, dammed part of the Colorado River in Austin, Texas. Here, harmful cyanobacteria often grow in mats on the bottom. Some mats can float up.
matTitle: The mystery starts below the surface.
matText: Clear-looking water can hide a bottom mat. A photo, a sensor or a satellite gives only part of the story. None can prove that the lake is safe.
phaseNotice: Try any station. Complete challenges and keep your evidence in your notebook.
notebookIntro: Keep a clue, a question, or an idea worth testing. Your notes stay in this browser. Export a copy to keep or share with your team.
privacy: No account. No tracking. Notes and progress stay in this browser on this device. They are never sent to us. Clearing browser data can erase them.
sourceIntro: Real evidence, with its limits in view. These are frozen copies of public records, not live lake conditions. Open a source to see where it came from.
sourceLimits: Measurements are not a lake safety rating. Some samples come from tributaries, the lake bottom or different depths. Check the place, date, sample type and quality flags before comparing them.
emptyNotebook: Your notebook is ready for its first clue. A good question counts as a finding.
mapCaption: Mapped shoreline: USGS NHD. Selected City monitoring locations. Schematic display; not for navigation.
coachText: Help students compare evidence, notice uncertainty and choose their own next test.
adaptText: Start with the lake configuration, then adapt source files and local science.
scienceStatus: Science review in progress. No current lake-safety advice is provided here.

imageGalleryText: Real images can help us ask questions. They cannot tell us whether a sample contains toxins. Microscope plates from the local study still need a scientist to check their names.
